principles: Machine mode stdout is a stable API surface, not a human transcript.
Human guidance remains valuable in text mode, but must never corrupt JSON stdout.
Fix the shared CLI output path so future commands inherit the contract.
Regression tests must execute real CLI child processes and JSON.parse stdout directly.
drivers: Dashboard and host-neutral adapters need direct JSON.parse without substring extraction.
Existing text-mode workflow hints should remain useful for human CLI users.
The change touches validation gates, so high-risk review and adversarial coverage are required.

options.name: shared-cli-json-mode-suppression
pros: One choke-point covers validate and future hint-decorated commands
Keeps handler code simple and preserves text mode hints
Matches dashboard contract without requiring adapter-side heuristics
cons: Requires careful test coverage to avoid accidentally suppressing text hints

options.name: validate-only-special-case
cons: Leaves future hint-decorated JSON commands vulnerable
Encodes policy in one handler path instead of CLI output contract

options.name: dashboard-substring-parser
cons: Makes dashboard depend on malformed output
Duplicates brittle parsing logic across consumers
Does not fix the underlying Lattice CLI contract bug

rationale: Choose the shared CLI JSON-mode suppression because the bug is an output contract violation at the CLI wrapper layer; dashboard and adapters should receive strict JSON stdout, while text-mode users keep next-step hints.

preMortem.scenario: JSON mode still receives a hint on failure paths
preMortem.trigger: validate --json returns allPass=false or coverage missing and validateHint emits remediation text
preMortem.consequence: dashboard fails exactly when it needs structured diagnostics most
preMortem.mitigation: Add failing/edge CLI smoke that JSON.parse stdout succeeds and stdout excludes next-step markers for JSON mode.

preMortem.scenario: Text mode loses useful next-step guidance
preMortem.trigger: implementation disables decorateResult for validate globally instead of only machine JSON mode
preMortem.consequence: human Lattice workflow becomes less ergonomic and reviewers lose next action hints
preMortem.mitigation: Regression smoke asserts non-json validate text output still contains the validation hint.

preMortem.trigger: machine mode detector checks args.json only
preMortem.consequence: commands using the documented --format=json contract remain inconsistent
preMortem.mitigation: wantsMachineJson must check args.json===true OR args.format==="json"; smoke covers at least one --format=json command.

preMortem.scenario: Tests pass by substring parsing instead of enforcing contract
preMortem.consequence: the bug can reappear while tests stay green
preMortem.mitigation: New smoke must call JSON.parse(stdout) directly and assert no trailing hint in stdout.
